title: Christ as Wisdom and the Eternal Dwellings
english: Deceptive doctrines constructed sophistically. They have surrounded me like bees [surround] wax, and the following: the genus of wax-makers is similar to bees; for although they are greater than bees in size, they do not deceive the unreasoning ones as bees do; nor do they make honey or mold wax, nor do they have a sting to repel those attempting to harm the wax. But eating the honey from the opposite, they wage war against the bees, just as those having used their own sting to safely destroy the wax-makers as having defiled their fruit.

The honey-making and wax-molding bee is not an allegory, but the Church which has honored the wisdom of God, whose labors, though not of a precious or glorious kind, are offered by kings and laymen for health; even though she is weak in strength, her preaching is not in persuasive words of human wisdom, but she possesses the sting in the demonstration of the spirit and power of God, having the word of faith, just as she destroys heresies like wax-makers, dividing them by the reproof of the truth. And one is the bee that has honored the wisdom, but many are those that depart from honoring the wisdom of God—not bees, but those who are like bees; he is not sinning, saying [they are] wax-makers surrounding like wax to consume the honey and having been burned like fire in thorns. For those from the heresies and the fire of shameful things and desires escape, as Paul says, 'For what is shameful to speak of is made known by them' (2 Cor 13:1). And the Gospel interpreted the thorns as pleasures.

However, even if they surrounded the wise one like wax, bees, and were burned like fire in thorns, they did not defend themselves by the name of the Lord alone. For he did not only remain undefiled, but he also cast down all their sophistical reasoning, and every high thing boasting itself against the knowledge of God, since his works are not fleshly but are powerful in God, not being defeated by the approach of God. The Lord becoming salvation does not receive a beginning of being; for he is both eternal and everlasting. And he becomes for salvation according to the taking up of the relation...

Regarding those being saved, God submits to the mind these things said by the one declaring that all things have become Christ; for it has not become [that] God is Word, not truth, not wisdom, not Son, but he has become to us wisdom, not merely having become wisdom, but this himself to us is righteousness and sanctification and redemption. For the reference to these things having become to us simply and eternally is said according to the relation toward us; thus God has made him both Christ and Lord, Christ meaning king and priest to those who reign and to those for whom he offers the sacrifices, but also to those who wish to serve him as Lord, and in general, the things said concerning him are not thought to be impieties.

You will understand the dwellings of the righteous, which are alone with the Father according to the fulfillment of the promises, concerning which the Savior says: 'When [Mammon] departs' (meaning that), 'they will receive you into the eternal dwellings' (Ps 117:15a). In these dwellings all the righteous are rejoicing; for they have attained the promised good things. Thus it is well said, 'A voice of joy and confession in the dwellings of the righteous' (Ps 117:15b), with sorrow and sighing fleeing away. And if you say that even the bodies of the righteous, their dwellings, will be returned to them incorruptible and spiritual, you will not dispute that in these dwellings of theirs there will also be a voice of joy and confession. A voice of joy and salvation is brought forward, as the righteous rejoice in the aforementioned dwellings having received the eternal salvation, not different from eternal life.

He has thus made power for those partaking of him, as it is possible to say, 'I can do all things in Christ who strengthens me' (Phil 4:13). He thus lifts up and exalts the one partaking, as one having been strengthened by the right hand of the Lord more brightly and more greatly, and to say a second time, 'The right hand of the Lord made power' (Ps 117:16). Therefore he says, 'I shall no longer die, he who follows the evil death, but I shall live' (Ps 118:17), partaking of the life opposite the evil death, in order to recount the wonderful works of God that have become in me. And his right hand makes power in everyone who thinks and acts according to the right, but also lifts him up as a second power in him of the former power, through which having obtained immortality, he says, 'I shall not die, but...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Gates of Law and Faith
english: I shall live, and the following. The gates were formerly the law and the prophets through which Israel entered toward God (Ps 117:19-20), but now the gate is faith, through which we are more closely brought near, being testified to by the law and the prophets. Into this understanding one should take also that which is said in Jeremiah: 'Stand in the paths and ask for the ancient well-trodden ways of the Lord, and examine what is the good way, and walk in it, and you will find cleansing for your souls.' For if someone stands here in the many paths—I mean the private virtues—he will examine those worn down from eternity by the saints, in order to know who, after this, according to the theory, is the good way; he who walks finds cleansing for his soul, having cleansed it through obedience to the truth.

Understand this (Ps 117:18-20): he who is being educated by divine discipline and most profitably by the Lord does not fall into the death that holds those who sin. For death encounters those who are uneducated, but he who is being educated by the Lord, having excellent thought and practice, is not handed over to the death that receives those handed over to the passions of dishonor and unproven mind. When the name of righteousness is being accused against every moral virtue, its gates—the private virtues—must be spoken of, into which those who are through asceticism and care for them enter, knocking at them. And they enter upon confessing those things which they have done outwardly, being of the gates of righteousness. He says 'into them' and not 'through them'; for one must not bypass the activities of the virtues, but must travel through them. But having entered into the gates of righteousness and having confessed within them, another gate is shown to be superior and more honorable, the one according to the theory of the truth, into which those having perfected righteousness enter, so as to be called righteous as a nickname from it.

I will praise you immediately having opened to me the gates of righteousness, and I thank you that you heard me and received the petition and provided salvation (Ps 117:21). For every day of sensation occurring under the sun, the sun may rise over the earth; the day shown under the sun of righteousness being the Lord was constructed, which they also, showing to one another, being illumined by the true light, say: 'This is the day which the Lord has made' (Ps 117:24); hence let us rejoice and be glad in it, as walking becomingly in the day; for we are no longer of night and darkness but sons of light and truth, having the faith of Abraham who rejoiced to see the day of the Lord (John 8:56), and rejoiced at having seen it.

Ps 117:25-26a: The one who has a conception of God takes forethought for all things from him, and demands both to be saved and to prosper; for God is a God of saving, and by him the steps of a man are directed (Ps 36:23).
Hence also in the first psalm the one being blessed prospers in all things whatsoever he does (Ps 1:3), using God as guide of the way leading to blessedness.

'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord' (Ps 117:26). And the Evangelists took this voice to be a prophecy concerning Christ; for he is truly the one who comes authoritatively and in the name of the Lord.

Ps 117:26b-27a: Though all the men before him together with angels came as servants of the Lord—indeed each said 'Thus says the Lord,' and each of the angels says to the one to whom he comes, 'The Lord sent me'—yet this one who comes in the name of the Lord is blessed.
Hence each of those who announced his sojourn beforehand says: 'We have blessed you from the house of the Lord' (Ps 117:26).
For the one coming is from the house of the Lord, from the Father's bosom.
For it is added immediately: 'God is the Lord, and he has appeared to us' (Ps 117:27). For his coming is not to change place but to appear, previously unseen.

For existing invisible by being the image of the invisible God (Col 1:15), having taken the form of a servant (Phil 2:7) and become the Word flesh (John 1:14), he was seen, that thus manifested he might lead by this contemplation unto also beholding his glory, 'glory as of the only-begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth' (John 1:14).
For those who have completed this initiation say: 'Even if we knew Christ according to the flesh, yet now we know him no longer' (2 Cor 5:16).

And it is well said 'the one coming,' but not 'the one who came'; for he always comes and sojourns with the race of men, even if not through flesh; not moved nor changing place himself—for he is unchangeable and unalterable, filling heaven and earth with divine presence.
But with us approaching him by relation and disposition [...].
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Blessedness of Seeking God's Law
english: Regarding His distance, some find Him coming near to them (Draw near to God and He will draw near to you [Ps 117:27bc]), while those who are distanced are not departing locally but, as I have previously said, by relationship; for God is far from the ungodly (Ps 117:27). And not in this way: they are pruning the shoots and the fruits just as they bear them.

In these things, not finding [them], establish a feast extending until the horns of the spiritual altar, from which, having taken a coal with tongs, the other of the seraphim is sent to the prophet to cleanse him and to take away his iniquities and his sins. But to whom is it commanded to establish a feast—the teachers and priests? Perhaps you will even say to the angels. But to do what is necessary and to think the truth is a feast established according to the guidance of God. This has especially much room among those who have cast off oldness in order to become a new planting.

And since the Passover is fulfilled in the month of the new [moons], it is possible to conceive that anyone passing from wickedness and the sensible things to virtue and the intelligible things, being renewed, prunes, so as to celebrate and to bring forward spiritual sacrifices, as those showing the altar to be royal by its horns. And if these things were said concerning our feast of the weeks, they would not be lacking truth (Ps 117:28-29).

He who is thanking God through the Psalm for having made such great and so many blessings proclaims: 'You are my God, and I will confess to you; you are my God, and I will exalt you' (Ps 118:2-3). Glorifying, theologizing you, I say: 'You have done wonderful things in me; for having exalted me and having made strength, so that I might not die but living, I might recount your works.' And second, I will confess that you heard my petitions and became my salvation. Having learned through experience your great mercy and your goodness, and exhorting others, I say to many, proclaiming: 'Confess to the Lord, what is good, what has mercy extending into the age, according to how he shows mercy by his much goodness' (Ps 118:2a). For if even the words of God were to testify to Him and to His truth.

Blessed then are those searching out his testimonies and seeking him with all their heart, turning away from all human haste and approaching him through good works and right understanding. But the blessing is not for those who have gone [away], but for those who are going; even though those working lawlessness in his law have not gone, it is evident that they have never attempted to test the divine law as if it were among them; for whoever sins lawlessly, lawlessly he shall perish. Nor are they those who have never heard the divine teaching; for those who, after being initiated into this, stumble, are said to have sinned against the law and to be transgressors of it.

Then I shall not be ashamed in keeping all your commandments; not on one thing, but on all (Ps 118:6). For according to those commandments I do not look, I shall be ashamed (Ps 118:8b). For I am often abandoned for a little while for the sake of testing and my trial, having bravely endured circumstances to be benefited. But immediately, with your helping, having run the race, I shall be crowned; therefore, so that I may not be defeated by those striving mightily, do not leave me exceedingly. He who does not receive the words of God from above and hides them in his heart, so that having made his mind and purpose according to these, is without sin before God who sees the hidden, not only not committing adultery but not even reaching for the shameful thing (Ps 118:11).

The Son also agrees with what is set forth: if, having received the word of my commandment, you hide it with yourself, your intellect will obey wisdom. So that I may not be glorified for nothing having had your judgments performed, repay me the divine and blessed life, so that living according to it I may keep your words; for after remembering them, to keep them following (Ps 118:17). To this end you will take that which was said by Jesus: 'He who holds my commandments and keeps them' (John 14:15/21); for he who remembers them also keeps them, doing them as well. Another, saying 'judgments' instead of 'rights/statutes', did not explain it thus: 'God's rights always benefit, being truly good. Desiring them at all times, he has loved them, not wanting to do them out of grief or out of necessity, as those do...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
